messages:
Alex (platform): heads up — proposing SDK + API headers to influence smart routing: region hint, tier override, and a debug flag. want to get buy-in before i draft the RFC
Marta (api): want the exact header names and precedence rules. also how this interacts with quotas?
Alex (platform): thinking: X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1 | us-east-1 (soft hint), X-Redwood-Tier: pro|enterprise|free (override allowed for internal tests), X-Redwood-Debug: true|trace (only allowed on non-prod keys)
Kevin (runtime): careful: allowing tier overrides from client could bypass customer routing SLOs. we should require the key to be authorized for tier overrides (signed flag on API key)
Samir (devex): +1 on key-level permission. also we need SDK ergonomics: prefer options object over raw headers for most users, but headers must exist for curl/debugging
Marta (api): agree re auth. name suggestions: maybe use newer prefix like Redwood-Region instead of X-? we try to avoid historic X- header baggage
Linh (telemetry): whichever we pick needs to be surfaced in telemetry and console. we want tags for region_hint, tier_override, and debug_flag so dashboards can group by them. also plan to add note to per-route cost breakdowns if override was used
Alex (platform): good call. how about: Redwood-Region, Redwood-Tier, Redwood-Debug. Implementation: API accepts both headers and request JSON fields; headers take precedence. default behavior: route by account tier -> region affinity -> model variant map. override flow only if key has override permission
Kevin (runtime): fallback behavior for model variants needs clarity. if region can't serve variant A, should we fallback to variant B in same region first, or route cross-region to preserve variant? prefer same-region variant B to avoid cross-region latency and data residency leaks
Marta (api): add a routing policy parameter? maybe Redwood-Routing-Policy: prefer-same-region|prefer-variant|force-region. defaults to prefer-same-region
Samir (devex): sdk example for JS could be: 
```js
// set region hint and request debug traces
const res = await client.generate({prompt}, {region: 'eu-west-1', debug: true});
// low-level header example
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  headers: {
    'Authorization': 'Bearer sk-...',
    'Redwood-Region': 'eu-west-1',
    'Redwood-Tier': 'enterprise'
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({model: 'rw-v1'})
});
```
Linh (telemetry): for debug traces please ensure we strip debug payloads from production logs unless key is in dev mode. debug flag should also return a small routing trace in response when allowed (short array of steps)
Alex (platform): routing trace idea is good for canary debugging. we should limit it to 5 steps and redact node identifiers. also add a header in response: Redwood-Routing-Trace: <tokenized> or provide via streaming event
Kevin (runtime): we need to update the fallback matrix: prefer same region variant (quantized/older) -> other compatible variant in same region -> cross-region same variant -> cross-region compatible variant -> fail (with suggested fallbacks). document compatibility table per model family
Marta (api): quota implications: if tier override is used to a higher tier, billing must still follow account billing. we should block usage that exceeds account quota even if a header asks for enterprise routing
Samir (devex): UX in console: show a per-request flag column so users can filter by region hints and overrides. when someone does a tier override in a workspace, show an audit entry and require an approval step for org-scoped keys
Linh (telemetry): agree. add metric labels: routing_hint, routing_override, routing_policy. create alert for anomalous number of overrides from a single key (possible abuse)
Marta (api): naming debate: Redwood-Tier values: use numeric slugs (tier=100/200) or semantic (free/pro/enterprise)? I prefer semantic for clarity in logs
Kevin (runtime): semantic is fine, but map internally to numeric for sorting and quota checks
Alex (platform): open questions: 1) header vs param precedence; 2) allowed values and fallback order; 3) key-level opt-in for overrides; 4) telemetry labels and retention; 5) console audit/approval workflow
Marta (api): action items: i'll sketch API surface and validation rules. Alex, can you write the runtime fallback matrix? Kevin, you'll add the compatibility table for model variants. Linh, draft metric names and retention. Samir, mock console UX for override approvals
Alex (platform): i'll draft RFC today, will include canary rollout plan: enable header parsing behind feature flag, default deny tier overrides, expose debug traces to dev keys only, run 2-week experiment on staging traffic
Kevin (runtime): once RFC done, we need unit tests for header parsing, integration test for fallback matrix (simulate region full), and a chaos test where preferred region is switched mid-request
Samir (devex): for SDK release: add opt-in debug param in 1.2.0, then headers in 1.3.0 after server rollout. update quickstart with header examples
Marta (api): one more: add a short response error code when fallback changed the variant, maybe 409-fallback-used with a hint header Redwood-Fallback-Reason
Linh (telemetry): add sample size cap on routing-trace for telemetry to avoid cardinality explosion
Alex (platform): great, i'll post the RFC link here when ready. thanks all :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: feature/route-headers parser -> staging (canary 10%) at 2024-04-01T16:00:00Z
Marta (api): receiving the canary, will monitor dashboards and audit logs
Kevin (runtime): ping me on pager if fallback rates > 1%
Alex (platform): end-to-end checklist in RFC, marking this thread resolved for now
